question.problem: Given that $X∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.6)$ and $Y∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.6)$ are independent, calculate $P(X=1\,\cup \,Y=0).$
question.worked_solution:
By the addition law, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=1\,\cup \,Y=0) & =P(X=1)+P(Y=0)-P(X=1\,\cap \,Y=0).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the multiplication law for independent events, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=1\,\cap \,Y=0) & =P(X=1)\cdot P(Y=0).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=1\,\cup \,Y=0) & =P(X=1)+P(Y=0)-P(X=1)\cdot P(Y=0).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $X∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.6),$ we have

$$
P(X=1)=0.6,\,P(X=0)=0.4,
$$

and since $Y∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.6),$ we have

$$
P(Y=1)=0.6,\,P(Y=0)=0.4.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=1\,\cup \,Y=0) & =P(X=1)+P(Y=0)-P(X=1)\cdot P(Y=0) \\  & =0.6+0.4-0.6\cdot 0.4 \\  & =1-0.24 \\  & =0.76.\end{aligned}
$$
